global_tips.text: A community member described common mystery packs as best for new collectors; her post said six prints and the buyer chooses the top print.
A community member said smaller mystery packs of four or five prints are easier to sell because buyers do not have to lay out as much money.
A community member warned smileys include fakes that look obviously bad, and said she is ~92% done tracking verified actuals. Treat unverified smileys carefully.

As of Sep 6 evening, a community member said only three of the numbered /100 smileys were accounted for; anything else is speculation. Separate discussion noted consecutive-number eBay listings and $300 sales.
Regular mini prints are 2.5×3.5 inches (standard art trading-card size) and fit standard sleeves and binders; Vault X binders were mentioned as fitting.
As of Sep 8 morning, a community member said they were starting an Excel-style list of all print variants; another was not aware of an existing list.
Community compares Mystery Pack vs Original/Emporium label variants on the same image; some variants (e.g. Dawn & Sunset) can look almost like a new print, and additional variants keep appearing.
OOC prints (e.g. Only NY 35mm per 2026-09-09 claim) are often said to need another OOC or multiple desirable prints for a fair trade.
Vault app can show how many collectors own a print; community uses that count to gauge rarity and ISO expectations, with the caveat that ownership does not imply a duplicate is available to trade.

Pop-up prints gated by long lines/limits (e.g. Snoopy/Harry) are sometimes weighed against limited paid sets (e.g. Guinness with spend requirement); community compared Guinness-set vs Snoopy-set trades.
Community advice to new collectors: look up print values and avoid trading rare prints for commons; commons tend to show up over time. Example cited: a NY-pizza unicorn traded for a common.
Merci Busy World Richard Scarry is discussed as a likely future unicorn due to overseas access barriers; community advises being picky in trades.
Blue-Footed Booby variants: community notes eye placement differences can make the bird head look turned.
Happy-mail trading guidance: match location prints with location prints and catalog with catalog; OOC often reserved for starred ISO requests.
Community reports Festive Collective as the only Chicago custom so far; Nashville Inciardi machines are often described as common catalog.

Early-October dibs train (about one week): locations, customs, and hot/rare commons, including current MPCC prints not yet in machines. Reported rules: first dibs; 10-minute posting window; replace stalled trains after 3 hours.
Community notes Vault/spreadsheet rarity labels can conflict with Emporium sightings (example: Blueberry labeled unicorn while reported at Emporium). Treat contested labels carefully.
Community framing (2026-09-11): Sept MPCC / catalog prints often requested 1:1 catalog↔catalog; customs listed separately rather than mixed into the 1:1 catalog ask.

Community opinion (2026-09-11, unverified): Harry Smiley may command a rare OOC in trade (examples cited: old Patagonia, Wash Arch) and some collectors argue it is rarer than Balloon Dog due to limited pop-up run and print limits.
Community pointer (2026-09-11): Emporium print list is referenced via the spreadsheet in the Facebook group’s pinned section.
2026-09-11 exhibit update: Peanuts/Snoopy prints being expanded toward US availability; NYC Snoopy in Style limited to one machine with a 2-print cap through Sep 26.
Community (2026-09-11, subjective): Ice Cream Sandi treated as catalog (once OOC, now in mystery packs / not in machines); roughly 1:1 vs another popular catalog or ice cream print.
Custom Philly prints announced for Eagles games starting Sunday 2026-09-13; community places the machine at Pepsi Plaza sections 107 & 113; token access still unclear.
Community (2026-09-11): Blue Lobster treated as OOC/rare and unlikely to sell openly; fair trade framed as OOC↔OOC; Pinecone called out as currently in multiple machines.
Messenger Print Variants (2026-09-11): Wall of Buoys may have a variant with an orange spot left of the red buoy; multiple variants speculated, unverified.
Community framing (2026-09-12): MPCC/catalog sought 1:1; harder-to-find/OOC customs may draw multi-for-one offers. Single-voice ISO, not consensus.
